chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Bukayr, from Suleyman al-Ja'fari, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: When you are in the evening and you look at the sun during its setting and departure, say: In the name of Allah, and by Allah, and all praise is for Allah, Who did not take a companion nor a son, and there was not for Him a partner in the dominion, and there was not for Him a guardian from the disgrace, and magnify Him with magnification.

And all praise is for Allah, Who is described but cannot be described, and He knows but cannot be known. He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal. And I seek refuge in the Face of Allah, the Generous, and by the Great Name of Allah, from the evil of what He created and scattered, and from the evil of what is beneath the earth, and from the evil of what is hidden and apparent, and from the evil of what I have described and what I have not described. And all praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds.

He mentioned that it is a security from every predatory beast, and from the accursed Satan and his offspring, and everything that bites or stings. And its reciter will not fear a thief nor a ghul (demon) when he speaks with it.

He said: I said to him, 'I am a hunter of wild beasts, and I spend the night in the ruins and I am alone.' So he said to me, 'Say when you enter: In the name of Allah, I enter, and enter with your right leg; and when you exit, exit with your left leg, and mention Allah, for you will not see anything disliked.'

key_terms.خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ: The treachery of the eyes (glances that betray inner thoughts)
key_terms.غُولًا: A type of demon or shapeshifter

ai.seo_question: What is the evening supplication for protection from beasts and demons according to Imam al-Rida (AS)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith outlines a comprehensive evening dhikr attributed to Imam al-Rida (AS), blending theological affirmations of divine unity with practical spiritual protection against unseen forces. The text highlights the Shia emphasis on specific verbal invocations as a means of securing safety from beasts, jinn, and thieves, particularly for those in solitary or hazardous environments. This practice underscores the interplay between reciting Quranic attributes and employing prophetic traditions for daily spiritual safeguarding.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Bukeyr, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary who said,
‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When it is evening, so look towards the sun during the setting and disappearing, so say,

‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who neither Took a female companion, nor a son, and there does not happen to be a match for Him<sup>azwj</sup> in the Kingdom, and there does not happen to be a guardian for him from the disgrace, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Greatness is the Greatest. 
And the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who Describes while He<sup>azwj</sup> cannot be described, and He<sup>azwj</sup> Knows while He<sup>azwj</sup> cannot be known. He<sup>azwj</sup> Knows the betrayal of the eyes and what the chests conceal. And I seek Refuge by His<sup>azwj</sup> Benevolent Face, and by the Magnificent Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, from the evil of what is spread and inseminated, and from the evil of what is beneath the ground, and from the evil of what is hidden and apparent, and from the evil of what can be described and what cannot be described. And the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds.

He<sup>asws</sup> mentioned: ‘It is a security from every predatory wild animals, and from the Pelted Satan<sup>la</sup> and his<sup>la</sup> offspring, and everything what bites or stings, and its reciter, when he speaks with it, would neither fear a thief nor a devil’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘I am a hunter of the wild animals and I tend to spend the night among the ruins and I am alone’. So heasws said to me: ‘Say when you enter (the hunting), ‘In the Name of Allahazwj I enter’, and enter your right leg; and when you exit, so exit your left leg (first) and Name Allahazwj (Bismillah), so you will not be seeing an abhorrence’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Bukayr from Sulayman al-Ja’fari who has said the following:

“I heard abu al-Hassan saying, ‘In the evening when you see the sun about to go down and disappear then say, “In the name of Allah, with (the help of) Allah, all praise belongs to Allah, Who has not taken any companion, or children. Who has no partner in His kingdom or a supporter against weakness, and He is greater than can be described,

all praise belongs to Allah Who describes (things) and Himself cannot be described. Who knows all things but Himself cannot be known. He knows the stealth glance of the eyes and whatever the chests hide. I seek protection with His honorable face, and with His great names against the evil of whatever He has spread and has populated, the evil of the things beneath the earth, the evil of what is apparent and that which is hidden, the evil of what I mentioned or did not mention, all praise belongs to Allah Lord of the worlds.”

“The Imam mentioned that this is protection against all the beasts, and all devils condemned to stoning and all the biting and stinging animals. One who reads this supplication should have no fear from thieves or the devils.’

“I (the narrator) then said to him, T hunt beasts and at night I sleep in ruined places and I feel afraid.’ He said on entering them say, ‘In the name of Allah, I enter and step your right foot first but when coming out step with your left foot first and mention the name of Allah you will not see any frightening thing.”’
